chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about whether walking is superior or riding. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man is affluent, and he walks in order to lessen his expenditure, then riding is superior for him.'
ai.seo_question: Is it better to walk or ride during Hajj if one is wealthy?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for an affluent individual, riding is superior to walking if the intent is to conserve wealth, as it prevents unnecessary expenditure while maintaining the status of a traveler. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that the virtue of walking is not absolute but contingent upon the intention of humility and frugality rather than mere physical exertion. The ruling underscores the balance between spiritual humility and practical stewardship of one's resources in acts of worship.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the walking being superior of the riding. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If a man is affluent, so he walks in order to lessen his expenditure, so (for him rather) the riding is superior’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about traveling for al-Hajj if on foot is more virtuous or riding. He (the Imam) said, ‘If one is affluent and he travels on foot to reduce his expenses then riding is more virtuous.’”
